summary: All four review issues fixed in the same checkout, preserving prior work. (1) setTool now ends the inline editor only on a real tool change — it derives the owning tool from editingMarkerIndex (marker vs text), so Text→Marker and Marker→Text commit the edit while re-selecting the owning tool leaves it open. (2) invalidateMarkerCursorPreview() now runs on every path that can change nextMarkerNumber: placement, undo/redo (via resetTransientSelectionState), clearAll, marker-tool delete, selection-tool delete, setTool, zoom-factor change, color change, and committed number edits; a test hook onMarkerCursorInvalidation verifies this headlessly. (3) currentColor gained a didSet that invalidates, covering the palette's direct `canvasView.currentColor =` writes (picker button, .selectColor keyboard shortcut, focus navigation, init all funnel through selectColor(index:)); setColor was reduced to a bare assignment to remove the redundant path. (4) MarkerItem.maxNumber = 999_999 caps numbering consistently: isSafeToRestore rejects numbers outside 1...cap, commitMarkerEditing rejects over-cap input, nextMarkerNumber returns Int? (guard maxNumber < cap before +1, so no overflow even for Int.max), and placement guards on nil to refuse rather than wrap. Targeted run: 24/24 marker tests pass; full suite: 253/253 pass.
findings: Palette color paths verified: every color change flows through EditorWindowController.selectColor(index:) → canvasView.currentColor = colors[index] (line 602), reached by colorPickerButtonPressed (595), the .selectColor editor action shortcut (704), colorFocusIndex navigation (720), and init (315). The didSet on currentColor covers all of them; no other assignment sites exist.

Marker number cap chosen as 999_999 (6 digits max, keeps the capsule reasonably sized). A restored marker at exactly the cap is safe but blocks further placement; cap-1 restores and places exactly the cap next.
nextMarkerNumber returns nil once the cap is reached; placement then redraws and returns without an undo snapshot — no crash, no wrap, no duplicate.

Int.max and 1_000_000 in a restored state are rejected by isSafeToRestore, so the overflow path is unreachable through normal decode — but nextMarkerNumber is still overflow-safe for any unexpected in-memory state.

Numeral/diameter sizing left as-is per the review note: diameter reuses defaultTextFontSize (same scaling calculation as text); numeral renders at ~0.55×diameter. Review confirmed 'same scaling is sufficient' for 'size scales like font of text'.

Invalidation hook onMarkerCursorInvalidation fires synchronously from invalidateMarkerCursorPreview; the window invalidateCursorRects call is a no-op in headless tests, so the hook is what the tests assert on.
Empty clearAll (items already empty) early-returns without invalidating — nextMarkerNumber is already 1 there, so nothing is stale.

No changes to EditorWindowController.swift or README.md in this round — existing palette code already assigns currentColor directly, which the didSet now covers.
decisions: Owner-aware tool-change check in setTool (editingTool = editingMarkerIndex != nil ? .marker : .text) rather than a tool whitelist — matches the actual ownership and stays correct if more editing tools appear.

currentColor.didSet as the single invalidation point for color — every write path (palette, setColor, direct assignment, future callers) is covered with zero redundancy; setColor's explicit invalidate call was removed.
Cap at 999_999: large enough to be effectively unreachable in normal use, small enough that Int parse, capsule width, and PNG metadata stay sane; also makes '999998' test states human-checkable.

nextMarkerNumber returns Int? instead of clamping — a nil forces callers to decide; placement refuses, cursor preview shows the cap number. Guard ordering (max < cap before +1) makes overflow impossible by construction, not just by validation.
Invalidation placed inside resetTransientSelectionState rather than on undo()/redo() individually — covers every snapshot-application path now and later.
